properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued July 29 at 3:46PM MDT until July 29 at 4:15PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 346 PM MDT, severe thunderstorms were located along a line from 7
miles northeast of Manila Village to 9 miles south of Strasburg, or
along a line from 27 miles east of Denver to 34 miles east of Denver,
moving northeast at 10 mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect considerable tree damage. Damage is likely to mobile
homes, roofs, and outbuildings.

Locations impacted include...
Northeastern Aurora, Bennett, Strasburg, Byers and Manila Village.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 3:31PM MDT until July 29 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Gold Mountain Burn Area in...
Southeastern Ouray County in southwestern Colorado...

* Until 700 PM MDT.

* At 331 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Gold Mountain Burn Area. Between 0.3 and 0.6
inches of rain have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in debris flow.
The debris flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms
producing flash flooding in and around the Gold
Mountain Burn Area.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around
the Gold Mountain Burn Area.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Ouray.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 3:27PM MDT until July 29 at 4:30PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 327 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms that produced
heavy rain across the warned area have ended, with weaker showers and
thunderstorms expected to move in from the west. Between 1 and 3
inches of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is up to 0.5
inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is expected to continue
until the water has a chance to recede.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, roads, and
normally dry washes, as well as other poor drainage and
low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of North Central Fremont County.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Tallahassee Creek, Cottonwood Creek, Squaw Creek, and their
tributaries.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 29 at 3:25PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 325 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a line of strong
thunderstorms extending from 10 miles north of Manila Village to 7
miles east of Arapahoe Park, or extending from 26 miles northeast of
Denver to 22 miles southeast of Denver, moving east at 10 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph and half inch size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Northeastern Aurora, Bennett, Manila Village and Watkins.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 3:22PM MDT until July 29 at 5:30PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
At 322 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain are ending across the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of
rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate up to 0.5 inches in 1
hour can be expected across southern portions of the warned area.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is expected to continue until the water
has a chance to recede.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, rural roads and
normally dry washes, as well as other poor drainage and
low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Victor.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
West Beaver Creek, Middle Beaver Creek, Wilson Creek and Bison
Creek their tributaries.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 29 at 3:16PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
At 316 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 7
miles southeast of Arapahoe Park, or 22 miles southeast of Denver,
moving northeast at 5 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph and pea size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor damage to outdoor objects is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of Southwestern Arapahoe, Northwestern Elbert
and Northeastern Douglas Counties.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 29 at 3:10PM MDT until July 29 at 6:15PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southern Larimer County in north central Colorado including
the Miller Fork area of the Cameron Peak Burn scar...

* WHEN...Until 615 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 310 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 0.5 and 0.75 inches of rain
have fallen.

- This includes the following streams and drainages...
North Fork Fish Creek, Big Thompson River, Grouse Creek, Cow
Creek, Black Creek, North Fork Big Thompson River and Miller
Fork. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Glen Haven.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 3:06PM MDT until July 29 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
FFWBOU

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Douglas County in northeastern Colorado...

* Until 600 PM MDT.

* At 306 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, gulches,
roads, and poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Western Castle Rock, Parker, Castle Pines and Perry Park.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
East Plum Creek, Dry Gulch, Cherry Creek, Jackson Creek, Watson
Park Creek, Happy Canyon Creek, Newlin Gulch, Gove Creek, Spring
Creek, Plum Creek, Bear Creek and Garber Creek.
